title: Root canal takeover: anaerobes win over time
topic: How a sealed, infected canal shifts from facultative to obligate-anaerobe dominance over ~3 years (Fabricius 1982 monkey model).

claims.claim: Study model: pulps mechanically devitalized, open to the mouth ~1 week, then sealed; initial samples at day 7 after sealing (16 canals, 2 monkeys) and final samples at day 90, 180 and 1060 (one monkey per time point); 3 monkeys, 24 canals, quantitative culture
claims.source: Fabricius L et al., Scand J Dent Res 1982;90:134-144 (PMID 6951255)

Sundqvist G, J Endod 1992;18:427-430 (PMID 9796509); Fabricius L et al., Scand J Dent Res 1982;90:134-144 (PMID 6951255; lower facultative proportion in final samples); Möller AJ et al., Scand J Dent Res 1981;89:475-484 (PMID 6951246). Inferred from the shift toward anaerobes over time; no abstract reports the day-7 composition, so the early bar share is illustrative

caption:
Who wins as a root canal infection ages?

Classic monkey model: pulps devitalized, left open ~1 week, then sealed. Facultatives lead early; as O₂ is used up, obligate anaerobes take over.
Final apical samples (day 90-1060): 85-98% of cultured cells were obligate anaerobes.
Drivers: low O₂, peptide food, species interactions. Scope: sealed, untreated canals (3 monkeys, 24 canals, culture).

Refs: Fabricius 1982, Scand J Dent Res; Sundqvist 1992, J Endod; Siqueira & Rôças 2022, Int Endod J
Animation is schematic: counts, early bar shares and the O₂ meter are illustrative; time compressed.
